Delivery objective: Deploy the owner-produced MOSAIC backend through external infrastructure automation.
Demonstrable outcome: A Cloud Run revision starts from approved configuration, mounts persistent file storage for SQLite and exposes only supported routes.
Dependencies: Existing development GCP and ADA environment
Parallel work: DATA-R1 can begin once the mounted SQLite paths and single-writer boundary are agreed.
Orchestrator gate: The MOSAIC owner supplies the backend source, build contract and Cloud Run-compatible bootstrap; developers make no repository changes.
Exit criteria: Image publication, Cloud Run rollout, persistent volume, GCS snapshot, catalogue validation and route-boundary tests pass.

Delivery objective: Persist ADK conversations plus MOSAIC users, tokens, workspaces and administrator assignments in separate SQLite files.
Demonstrable outcome: An administrator provisions a user and atomic Skills; metadata and completed conversations survive Cloud Run instance replacement.
Parallel work: The MOSAIC owner may implement ADK and MOSAIC SQLite work in parallel after the mounted paths are available.
Orchestrator gate: All DATA-R1 stories change the MOSAIC repository and are owner-only.
Exit criteria: ADK and MOSAIC SQLite tests pass on the mounted filesystem; only the MOSAIC process opens the files for writing.

Demonstrable outcome: Browser cookies and human bearer tokens produce the same trusted user context and spoof attempts fail.
Parallel work: The external Dash shell can proceed against the published authentication and API contract.
Orchestrator gate: All authentication middleware and backend routes are implemented by the MOSAIC owner.
Exit criteria: Authentication, redaction and identity-spoof tests pass.

Delivery objective: Expose owned persistent conversations and controlled invocation lifecycle.
Demonstrable outcome: A user can create, stream, disconnect, reopen and cancel without accessing another user's sessions.
Parallel work: The standalone UI can build navigation against the published API while the MOSAIC owner implements the backend lifecycle.
Orchestrator gate: All API-R1 and ORCH-R1 changes are owner-only; external developers consume the contract.
Exit criteria: API contract, ownership, streaming, disconnect and 409 behaviour pass.

Delivery objective: Complete the pilot user journey and enforce workspace Skills.
Demonstrable outcome: The independently deployed Dash UI streams results through /api/v1 while MOSAIC applies the user's workspace at each new Goal.
Parallel work: The external Dash application and owner-only Goal binding can proceed in parallel against the published contracts.
Orchestrator gate: The MOSAIC owner alone implements Goal binding; the frontend makes no MOSAIC repository change.
Exit criteria: UI journeys pass; next-Goal Skill changes and in-flight stability pass.

Delivery objective: Make the invited development pilot repeatable and supportable.
Demonstrable outcome: The complete read-only journey is demonstrated from Cloud Run deployment through revision or instance replacement.
Parallel work: External black-box tests can start early; the MOSAIC owner maintains repository documentation.
Orchestrator gate: The MOSAIC owner accepts runtime behaviour and performs every MOSAIC README or source change.
Exit criteria: All acceptance criteria pass and the README records limitations.

Delivery objective: Replace pilot identity and storage constraints.
Demonstrable outcome: OIDC, service identities, PostgreSQL and multiple Cloud Run instances operate through the same trusted contracts.
Workstreams: Access and API; Backend and data
Parallel work: External infrastructure preparation may proceed, but identity, persistence adapters and replica coordination remain owner-only.
Orchestrator gate: ID-F1 and SCALE-F1 require MOSAIC repository changes and are owned by the MOSAIC owner.
Exit criteria: Pilot tokens and SQLite dependencies are removable.

Delivery objective: Select and prove the prescribed RAG platform without modifying MOSAIC.
Demonstrable outcome: An approved external prototype ingests controlled operational knowledge and returns cited context for the database investigation use case through a documented contract.
Dependencies: Release 1; ADA team guidance; development AI access layer
Parallel work: The evaluation and PoC can run alongside production identity work once ADA access and the non-sensitive sample corpus are available.
Orchestrator gate: No MOSAIC change is permitted. The MOSAIC owner reviews the integration contract and owns any later runtime adapter.
Exit criteria: ADA's position is recorded; the platform decision is approved; embedding, insert, update, delete and retrieve paths work; the database use case is measured; the PoC and MOSAIC integration contract are documented.

Delivery objective: Move Public Skill discovery and selection to users.
Demonstrable outcome: Users browse and manage Skills through a separately deployed Skills service and frontend.
Parallel work: Catalogue API and UI can proceed in parallel.
Orchestrator gate: External teams build the standalone service; any MOSAIC adapter or Goal-time change is owner-only.
Exit criteria: Manual pilot assignment is no longer required.

Delivery objective: Enforce platform identity and RBAC at provider boundaries.
Demonstrable outcome: Vendor MCP servers receive trusted context through the reusable shim and apply platform-specific policy.
Parallel work: Reference shim and first provider adapter can overlap after the header contract.
Exit criteria: Sensitive production data cannot cross user boundaries.

Delivery objective: Replace GCS JSON delivery and add governed visual authoring.
Demonstrable outcome: Approved relational publications feed runtime configuration and a separate workbench manages drafts.
Parallel work: Workbench shell can begin while registry publication stabilises.
Orchestrator gate: External teams build the registry and workbench; the MOSAIC owner alone implements runtime consumption.
Exit criteria: The GCS JSON snapshot is retired and publication is auditable.

Delivery objective: Add controls justified by scale and usage.
Demonstrable outcome: Retention, exact rate limits, resilience, observability, chargeback and advanced Goal controls meet approved policies.
Parallel work: Operational controls are independent except for shared telemetry contracts.
Orchestrator gate: Retention, rate limiting and Goal changes that touch MOSAIC are owner-only; external SRE and FinOps work remains assignable.
Exit criteria: Production support and governance targets are met.
